topPRs.title: eth/076-080: Unichain Mainnet migration tasks
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
The Unichain Mainnet migration ceremony in five tasks, mirroring the Sepolia set (#1563) plus the L1Splitter handover that only exists on mainnet. eth/077 sets the OP Enterprise batcher and unsafe block signer (cutover steps 2 and 3), signed by the FoundationUpgradeSafe, which becomes the SystemConfig owner with eth/074 (#1560). eth/078 rotates the `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` (5) proposer (cutover step 4) and eth/080 points the OperatorFeeVault at the OPE cost recipient on L1; both are signed by the L1PAO.

Unichain's Sequencer, Base and L1 fee vaults pay into Uniswap's FeeSplitter, whose L1-fee leg is the `Ownable2Step` L1Splitter `0x4300c0d3c0d3c0D3c0d3C0D3c0d3C0D3C0D30003`, owned by the alias of the Unichain SystemConfig owner Safe `0x9245d5D10AA8a842B31530De71EA86c0760Ca1b1`. eth/076 is that Safe starting the handover (`transferOwnership(alias(L1PAO))` via a portal deposit; named explicitly in `[addresses]` so it still resolves after eth/074 moves the SystemConfig), and eth/079 is the L1PAO accepting it and setting the recipient to the cost recipient with a 0.15 ETH minimum (eth/062 value). Both use `SetL1SplitterConfig` and the type-5 `SetDisputeGameArgs` support from #1562, which this PR is stacked on. The other splitter legs (`…0001`, `…0002`, `…0004`) are not touched.

Placeholders and open points: the OPE batcher, sequencer, proposer and cost recipient are `0xdead…0001` to `…0004`; the new L1Splitter owner (aliased L1PAO) is pending confirmation; the L1Splitter holds about 6 ETH below its 10 ETH minimum, which the lower minimum would let anyone withdraw to the new recipient; and the L1PAO tasks need the Maintenance Upgrade governance post. All tasks are DRAFT. Nonces are pinned to the live values on 2026-10-01 in stack order (eth/076 Unichain Safe 12, after eth/074; eth/077 FUS 73; eth/078-080 L1PAO 44-46 / FUS 74-76 / SC 71-73). Calldata was re-derived independently with `cast`, and `just simulate-stack` passes on both signing paths.

topPRs.title: eth/081-083: Soneium Mainnet migration tasks
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
The Soneium Mainnet migration ceremony in two tasks, same shape as Minato (#1565). eth/081 sets the OP Enterprise batcher and unsafe block signer (cutover steps 2 and 3), signed by the FoundationUpgradeSafe, which becomes the SystemConfig owner with eth/075 (#1561). eth/082 rotates the `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` (5) proposer (cutover step 4), signed by the L1PAO. On Soneium Mainnet type 5 is the respected and only game type (no type 9), so this rotation is blocking for the cutover; post-U20 there is no challenger to rotate.

eth/083 moves the L1FeeVault and OperatorFeeVault from Sony's Safe `0x34ffF1A1CB3C054E9eD1BbD36883B14A66E6C260` (set by eth/072) to the OPE cost recipient on L1 with a 0.15 ETH minimum (eth/062 values, 6 deposits), signed by the L1PAO and stacked after eth/082 (L1PAO 48 / FUS 79 / SC 75). The Sequencer and Base vaults stay on Sony's Safe. The cost recipient is the `0xdead…1004` placeholder.

The OPE batcher, sequencer and proposer are `0xdead…1001` to `…1003` placeholders, so both tasks are DRAFT; eth/082 also needs the Maintenance Upgrade governance post. Stacked on #1564 because the FoundationUpgradeSafe, L1PAO and Security Council nonces follow eth/077-080: eth/081 FUS 77, eth/082 L1PAO 47 / FUS 78 / SC 74 (live 2026-10-01: 44 / 73 / 71). Soneium cuts over after U21 Mainnet: once the U21 tasks exist, these pins and hashes move, the tasks may need renumbering after them, and if U21 redeploys the type-5 game the impl changes too. Calldata was re-derived independently with `cast`, and `just simulate-stack` passes on both signing paths.

topPRs.title: feat(template): SUPER_PERMISSIONED proposer rotation in SetDisputeGameArgs + new SetL1SplitterConfig
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
Two template changes needed by the Unichain and Soneium migrations. After U20 the only permissioned game left is `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` (5), whose `gameArgs` are `anchorStateRegistry(20) | proposer(20)` with no challenger, and `SetDisputeGameArgs` rejected anything but types 0, 1 and 8. It now accepts type 5 with that 40-byte layout: a row may only set `impl`, `anchorStateRegistry`, `proposer` and `bond` (which must be 0, as the v8.0.0 OPCM requires), the `l2ChainId()` impl check is skipped because super games have none, and the existing types are unchanged (their regression fixture still passes byte for byte). A proposer rotation is the same field-diff row the Ink migration used, with `gameType = 5` and only `proposer` set.

`SetL1SplitterConfig` is new. Unichain's fee vaults pay into Uniswap's FeeSplitter, whose L1-fee leg is the `L1Splitter` at `0x4300c0d3c0d3c0D3c0d3C0D3c0d3C0D3C0D30003` (unichain-contracts `src/FeeSplitter/L1Splitter.sol`, `Ownable2Step`, owned by the alias of an L1 Safe). No existing template covers it: `L1PortalExecuteL2Call` sends one deposit with no L2 checks, and the handover needs `acceptOwnership()` followed by up to three setters from the new owner. The template sends one portal deposit per call, in order, from the root Safe (`ProxyAdminOwner` by default, overridable with `safeAddressString`): either leg A (setters, then `transferOwnership(alias(newOwnerToAlias))`) or leg B (`acceptOwnership()`, then setters). Like `SetFeeVaultConfig` it requires an `l2RpcUrl` pre-flight that checks the aliased root is the `owner()` / `pendingOwner()`, skips unchanged values, dry-runs every call as the aliased root and asserts the resulting state, and `_validate` re-derives every deposit byte for byte. `simulatePendingOwnerTransfer` lets a leg-B task simulate before leg A has landed on L2; the README of any task using it must carry a `pendingOwner()` pre-execution check.

Examples and fixtures: `test/tasks/example/eth/049-set-dispute-game-args-super-permissioned` (Soneium type-5 proposer to a synthetic address) and `050-set-l1-splitter-config` (leg B on Unichain mainnet with synthetic recipient/minimum/interval), both pinned at L1 block 26096434, with regression tests `testRegressionCallDataMatches_SetDisputeGameArgsSuperPermissioned` and `testRegressionCallDataMatches_SetL1SplitterConfig` (L2 fork pinned at 60099000 via a test-only harness). Calldata of both examples, and of a leg-A run from the Unichain SystemConfig owner Safe, was re-derived independently with `cast`. The full `RegressionTest` suite passes locally against archive RPCs.

topPRs.title: sep/112-114: Unichain Sepolia migration tasks
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
The Unichain Sepolia migration ceremony in three tasks. sep/112 sets the OP Enterprise batcher and unsafe block signer on the SystemConfig (cutover steps 2 and 3), signed by the Sepolia FoundationUpgradeSafe, which becomes the SystemConfig owner with sep/110 (#1560). sep/113 rotates the proposer of the `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` (5) game (cutover step 4) and sep/114 points the OperatorFeeVault at the OPE cost recipient on L1 (recipient, network L2 to L1, 0.15 ETH minimum as in eth/062); both are signed by the L1PAO.

Post-U20 there is no challenger in any game type on Unichain Sepolia (type 5 has only a proposer, type 9 is permissionless), so unlike the Ink migration there is no challenger field to keep; the proposer rotation uses the type-5 support added to `SetDisputeGameArgs` in #1562, which this PR is stacked on. The Sequencer, Base and L1 fee vaults pay into Unichain's fee splitter and are untouched. Unlike mainnet, Unichain Sepolia's L1-fee leg (`0x03060844a69Ce66d756abc4b082B526780603220`) is an immutable contract with no owner or setters, so there is no L1Splitter handover on this network.

The OPE batcher, sequencer, proposer and cost recipient are not generated yet, so the tasks use `0xdead…0001` to `…0004` placeholders, are DRAFT, and their hashes will be regenerated once the real addresses are in. Nonces are pinned to the live values on 2026-10-01 in stack order: sep/112 FUS 77 (with a SystemConfig owner override standing in for sep/110), sep/113 L1PAO 57 / FUS 78 / SC 71, sep/114 L1PAO 58 / FUS 79 / SC 72. Calldata was re-derived independently with `cast`, and `just simulate-stack` passes on both signing paths.
